nodes.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.* By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. *See standard 1.OA.6 for a list of mental strategies.
nodes.label: 2.OA.B.2

nodes.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on ; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).
nodes.label: 1.OA.C.6

nodes.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
nodes.label: 1.OA.C.5

nodes.description: Fluently add and subtract within 5.
nodes.label: K.OA.A.5

nodes.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.
nodes.label: K.OA.A.2

nodes.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.
nodes.label: 1.OA.B.4

nodes.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).
nodes.label: K.OA.A.3

edges.reason: Addition facts support a fast inverse strategy and checks. Crossing out objects or counting back computes a difference without invoking the matching addition fact.
Subtraction within ten contains the smaller subtractions within five as cases of the same subtraction operation.
The 9-plus case is an easy make-ten example, while 8+5 can directly split 5 into 2 and 3 using the general method. Keep practice preparation without requiring an earlier fact family.
Earlier teen subtraction builds regrouping fluency. A break-ten calculation for 13 minus 4 or the matching 4-plus fact is a direct alternative to first mastering the 8/7/6 family.
edges.scope: extending regrouping subtraction to small subtrahends

edges.reason: The part-whole criterion expressly represents joining by addition; the written two-digit subtraction algorithm is the wrong prerequisite. The scope is operation meaning rather than a required count range. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: The joining meaning of addition in the explicit part-plus-part-equals-total relation

edges.reason: The part-whole criterion expressly represents the missing part through subtraction, without needing a column algorithm. The scope is operation meaning rather than every within-ten fact. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: The take-away meaning of subtraction in the explicit total-minus-part relation
